correctness.rationale: For q=3, an edge change at one coordinate has distance-vector displacement 1_B-1_C, for mutually disjoint equality blocks B and C. All nonzero patterns fall into the three exhaustively listed coordinate-partition cases; +1_B, -1_B, and 1_B-1_C uniquely recover every status count c_(π,B). Round d colors determine all marker-distance vectors, so round d+1 determines each neighbour-displacement multiplicity; consequently refinement separates all pointwise-stabilizer orbits. Standard wreath-product automorphisms show orbit invariance and classify the profiles. Stars-and-bars and multinomial counting yield the number and size formulas. Exact executable checks cover 985 mark configurations through dimension four, with finite limitations acknowledged.

originality.rationale: The archived own-claim comparison identified binary hypercube arbitrary-marker and q-ary Hamming two-marker orbit results, both proper subdomains. Indexed research queries and available primary literature reveal known Hamming automorphism structure and generic refinement/individualization concepts, but no source whose proved statement covers exact orbit recovery for every number of individually marked ternary vertices, the displacement inversion, or class-size formula. The original contribution is the all-marker ternary structural refinement theorem, not the known automorphism group or existing special cases. Specialist earlier coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: No independently performed publication-priority audit; a specialized Hamming graph Godsil/Tinhofer theorem might imply orbit equality even if not identified in the inspected literature.
The Boutin 2009 complete body was not accessible for inspection, but its available abstract addresses binary graph determining numbers, not this ternary counting-refinement statement.
Full source of Jones 2010 was accessible only as an excerpt and arXiv source listing; its standard wreath-product group fact is separately mathematically reconstructible.
The theorem concerns only alphabet size three and within-graph orbit recovery; it does not identify the colored graph among arbitrary competitors.

value.rationale: Ternary Hamming graphs form the smallest nonbinary Cartesian complete-graph powers. For arbitrary individually marked vertex configurations, the theorem completely determines the stable counting-logic partition, how many types occur and their cardinalities, and gives a bounded-round constructive reconstruction method. It extends both the known binary arbitrary-marker and the nonbinary two-marker special cases, resolving a natural structural orbit-recovery problem for an infinite family rather than an arbitrary finite invariant.
